title: The Word-Chain Machine Brain
subtitle: A child-friendly introduction to large language models
coreQuestion: How does a large language model answer questions?
learningGoals: Know that a large language model learns patterns from lots of text.
Know that it organizes answers from context instead of truly knowing everything like a person.
Learn that clearer questions usually lead to more helpful answers, and important answers need checking.
misconceptions: AI understands everything exactly like a human.
AI only answers by searching the internet every time.

hero.title: The Word-Chain Machine Brain
hero.lead: A large language model is like a machine that learned many language patterns. Give it a prompt, and it builds an answer step by step.
hero.sceneExplanation: The main visual is a friendly language machine: books, story cards, and question bubbles enter on the left; word networks and glowing nodes work in the middle; answer bubbles come out on the right. Tapping each step shows: read lots of text — learn patterns — read your prompt — build an answer — check important facts.
hero.childPrompt: Give the machine a clearer question and see if it can help better.
hero.parentPrompt: The key idea is safe AI literacy: AI can organize answers from learned patterns, but it can still be wrong. Avoid saying AI thinks exactly like a person.

classificationGroups.name: Input
classificationGroups.childExplanation: Your question, story, or request is the input.
classificationGroups.parentNote: This corresponds to a prompt, but the English term is not required at first.
classificationGroups.misconception: AI cannot always guess what you mean if you do not say it clearly.

classificationGroups.name: Language patterns
classificationGroups.childExplanation: AI learns how words and sentences often go together from lots of text.
classificationGroups.misconception: AI is not a perfectly correct encyclopedia inside a machine.

classificationGroups.name: Context
classificationGroups.childExplanation: What you said earlier can affect what AI says next.
classificationGroups.parentNote: Use a word-chain game to explain context.
classificationGroups.misconception: AI answers are affected by the current conversation.

classificationGroups.name: Output
classificationGroups.childExplanation: AI puts words together step by step into an answer.
classificationGroups.parentNote: Generated output is not the same as verified truth.
classificationGroups.misconception: A smooth answer is not always a correct answer.

classificationGroups.name: Check
classificationGroups.childExplanation: Important questions should be checked with adults or reliable sources.
classificationGroups.parentNote: This sets a safety boundary for children using AI.
classificationGroups.misconception: AI can sound confident and still be wrong.

representativeObjects.name: Question card
representativeObjects.childExplanation: The clearer your question is, the easier it is for AI to help.
representativeObjects.visualHint: a card with a question mark
representativeObjects.commonMisread: Thinking a very short question always works well.

representativeObjects.name: Story card
representativeObjects.childExplanation: You can give AI a story and ask it to continue or organize it.
representativeObjects.commonMisread: Thinking AI knows background you did not tell it.

representativeObjects.name: Word network
representativeObjects.childExplanation: Words have relationships. AI learns many of these relationships.
representativeObjects.commonMisread: Thinking the network is a real human brain.

representativeObjects.name: Pattern gears
representativeObjects.childExplanation: Patterns help turn input into a possible answer.
representativeObjects.commonMisread: Thinking patterns are the same as facts.

representativeObjects.name: Chat bubbles
representativeObjects.childExplanation: The same sentence can mean different things in different conversations.
representativeObjects.commonMisread: Only looking at the last sentence.

representativeObjects.name: Answer bubble
representativeObjects.childExplanation: AI organizes its answer into sentences for you.
representativeObjects.commonMisread: Thinking smooth sentences must be true.

representativeObjects.name: Check badge
representativeObjects.commonMisread: Thinking confident words mean correct facts.

mechanism.title: How does a large language model answer?

steps.childExplanation: It has learned from many sentences, stories, and question-answer examples.
steps.parentNote: Do not imply specific data sources. Keep it conceptual.

steps.childExplanation: It learns which words often go together and what a complete answer may look like.
steps.parentNote: This is the core: pattern learning, not human-like understanding.

steps.childExplanation: The clearer you are, the easier it is for AI to answer in the right direction.
steps.parentNote: Teach the child to ask clearer questions.

steps.shortTitle: Builds the answer step by step
steps.childExplanation: It works like a word-chain game, adding words into an answer.
AI can be wrong. Important questions need an adult or reliable source.
steps.parentNote: This is the safety baseline for children.

comparePairs.title: Large language model vs Search

a.name: Large language model
points: organizes answers from learned language patterns
can rewrite, summarize, and continue writing

comparePairs.childConclusion: AI and search can both help, but we need to check important things.

comparePairs.title: Clear question vs Vague question
comparePairs.childConclusion: Clearer questions make answers more useful.

comparePairs.title: Smooth answer vs Correct answer
comparePairs.childConclusion: A smooth AI answer still needs checking if it is important.

clickTasks.title: Which question is clearer?
clickTasks.prompt: A clear question helps AI answer better.

options.label: Tell me three forest animals and how they protect themselves

wrongHints.vague: This question is too broad. Try saying what kind of answer you want.

clickTasks.successCopy: Right! A clear question gives AI a better direction.

clickTasks.title: Is everything AI says always true?

options.label: Important things should be checked again
No, so we should never use AI

wrongHints.always-true: AI can make mistakes. Important things need checking.
wrongHints.never-use: AI can help, but we need to use it carefully.

clickTasks.successCopy: Good judgment! AI can help, and important answers should be checked.

clickTasks.title: Find: which things need checking again?
clickTasks.successCopy: You found the careful-use cases. Important facts need checking.
clickTasks.wrongHint: Think about health, money, and school facts: these should be checked.

clickTasks.title: How AI answers

options.label: Build an answer step by step

clickTasks.successCopy: You built the AI answer flow.
clickTasks.wrongHint: AI first learns from lots of text, then reads your prompt.

speakTemplates: AI is like ____. It answers using ____.
I can change ‘____’ into a clearer question: ‘____’.
If AI answers about ____, I should ____.
parentTips: Avoid saying AI thinks like a person or understands everything.
Encourage the child to turn vague questions into clear questions.
Set safety boundaries: health, safety, money, privacy, and school facts need checking.
acceptanceCriteria: The child can explain that AI answers from learned patterns.
The child understands that important answers need checking.
The child can improve a vague question into a clearer one.
